data:
An agent that calls an API directly has to hold the credential, which puts it in the model’s context window, its logs and its history. With apigent, the agent runs a saved request by name; apigent fills in the secrets at send time and masks them in everything it prints.
agentapigent run "get-user" --env staging {"ok":true,"status":200,"url":"https://api.example.com/users?api_key=*****","body":{"id":"u-123","auth":"Bearer *****"}, ...}
data.set-up-once-as-a-human#Set up once, as a:
The agent should only ever see names. Store secrets yourself, once:
apigent collection create "payments-api" --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --secret API_KEY=sk-live-... apigent save "list-payments" '{{BASE_URL}}/payments' --collection payments-api \ --auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' # The agent only needs: agentapigent run "list-payments" For environments, read the secret from stdin so it never lands in shell history: apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY.
data.start-here#Start here: Agent mode — turn on JSON output, no prompts and strict masking with --agent, APIGENT_AGENT=1 or an agentapigent symlink. Run apigent docs first. JSON output — the run --json object, dry runs, errors, history, diff and exit codes. MCP server: serve saved requests as tools to Claude, Cursor or any MCP client with apigent mcp. Memory safety — why credentials must stay out of context windows, and what apigent does about it.
data.what-the-agent-sees-and-what-it-doesnt#W: Direct curl apigent in agent mode API key in the command yes no — only a request name and environment name Credential headers in output yes ***** Secrets echoed back in the response body yes ***** Secrets in error messages yes ***** Record of what happened no every run recorded with secrets masked; apigent diag

data: Agent mode makes apigent safe and predictable for an AI agent: every command that can print JSON does, nothing ever prompts, and secrets are masked everywhere, including response bodies.
data.a-recommended-agent-loop#A recommended a: agentapigent docs — learn the commands. agentapigent list, agentapigent env list, agentapigent collection list — discover what exists. agentapigent show or agentapigent collection show — inspect before running. agentapigent run --env --dry-run — check that every placeholder resolves. agentapigent run --env — run the smallest request that answers the task. On failure: agentapigent diag . Use --persist only when the task explicitly needs extracted values saved. Keep secrets out of commands: an agent should never pass a token with --var (the token is then in its context anyway). Have a human store it once in an environment or collection: apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: Code Meaning 0 Success. A non-2xx response is still 0 unless --fail is passed (ok is false in the JSON). 1 Error: request or environment not found, resolution problems, transport error, script or extraction error, failed assertion, non-2xx with --fail, dry run with problems 2 Usage: missing argument with --no-input, conflicting flags (--persist --dry-run), --reveal / --output / paste / codegen --clipboard in agent mode, shell with --no-input other apigent exec exits with the child command’s code
data.no-prompts---no-input#No prompts: --no-i:
--no-input (or APIGENT_NO_INPUT=1) is implied by --agent and by --json. A command that would ask fails and says what to pass instead:
{"ok":false,"error":"request name is required: apigent run (list names with: apigent list --json)"} Other examples: saving into a collection that doesn’t exist, collection delete without --force, a missing passphrase (pass --passphrase or set APIGENT_IMPORT_PASSPHRASE), env set KEY=- on a terminal.
data.running-requests-run---json#Running requ:
stdout carries one JSON object per execution and nothing else (NDJSON for --chain steps and --data rows):
{"id":"e7770aa1-94f2-4b4a-9e3e-8605e5c1a0cc","short_id":"e7770aa1","request":"get-user","environment":"dev", "ok":true,"method":"GET","url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****","status":200,"status_text":"OK", "duration_ms":4,"size_bytes":89,"response_headers":{"Content-Type":"application/json","Set-Cookie":"*****"}, "body":{"id":"u-123","auth":"Bearer *****"},"extracted":{"uid":"u-123"}} (Wrapped for reading; real output is one line.) The agent checks ok, reads body, and on failure reads error, failure_phase and problems, then calls apigent diag . The full field list, problem kinds and failure phases are in JSON output.
data.see-also#See also: JSON output Memory safety for AI agents apigent exec — hand an environment to a script without printing it
data.step-1-read-apigent-docs#Step 1: read ap:
The first command an agent should run:
agentapigent docs # JSON: {"commands":[...],"sections":{...}} apigent docs # the same reference as compact text (~25KB) apigent docs run # one command It lists every command and subcommand with arguments and flags (type, default, aliases), generated from the binary itself, plus short sections on placeholders, scope precedence, extract rules, --persist, agent mode, the run --json shape, exit codes, exec and diag. See apigent docs.
data.strict-masking#Strict masking:
Outside agent mode, apigent already masks secrets in everything it shows or stores about a request: saved requests, dry runs, execution records, and the URL, headers and errors of run --json. Response bodies are shown as received, because they are your API’s data.
Agent mode also masks the body, response headers and errors, and exec output. “Secret” here means:
variables marked secret in an environment or collection, including values reached through an alias; variables whose names look sensitive (*key*, *token*, *secret*, *password*, *signature*, Authorization, Cookie, …); literal credentials written into the saved request: sensitive headers, sensitive query parameters (?api_key=…), auth params; the URL-escaped and JSON-escaped spellings of all of the above. Values shorter than 4 characters are not replaced inside free text. Details: Secret masking.
data.turn-it-on#Turn it on:
Use any one of these:
apigent --agent run "get-user" --env staging # flag, in any position APIGENT_AGENT=1 apigent run "get-user" # environment variable ln -s "$(command -v apigent)" ~/.local/bin/agentapigent agentapigent run "get-user" # binary named agentapigent The symlink is the most robust choice: give the agent agentapigent and it cannot forget the flag.
data.what-agent-mode-changes#What agent mode: Behaviour In agent mode Output --json is on for every command that has it: run, run --dry-run, diag, list, show, env list/show, history, timeline, diff, collection list/show, docs Prompts --no-input is on: commands never prompt; they fail and name the flag or argument to pass Errors Every error is printed on stdout as {"ok":false,"error":"..."} (and on stderr), usage errors included; help text is not printed on a usage error Masking Secrets are masked in response bodies, response headers and errors too (run, diag, diff), and in the output of exec child processes Refused (exit 2) --reveal, paste, codegen --clipboard, run --output; apigent shell refuses to start

data: Every command an agent or script needs has --json. In agent mode it is on automatically. Empty fields are omitted, and <, > and & are not escaped.
data.diag#diag: apigent diag --json prints {"record": {...}, "compared_with": ...}: the stored execution record (method, URL, headers, body, vars with name/origin/value, response headers, error, failure phase, assertions) and the comparison with the last success. See apigent diag.
data.diff#diff: apigent diff "get-user" --json {"request":"get-user", "before":{"id":"…","short_id":"699120a5","time":"…","status":200}, "after":{"id":"…","short_id":"e7770aa1","time":"…","status":200}, "format":"json","identical":true} When the responses differ, JSON bodies are compared as structured RFC 6902 changes; other bodies as a text diff.
data.errors#Errors:
With --json (or in agent mode), an error that is not part of an execution object — unknown request or environment, conflicting flags, a missing argument with --no-input — prints on stdout:
{"ok":false,"error":"request not found: nope"} The message also goes to stderr.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: Code Meaning 0 Success. A non-2xx response is still 0 unless --fail is passed. 1 Not found, resolution problems, transport error, script or extraction error, failed assertion, non-2xx with --fail, dry run with problems 2 Usage: missing argument with --no-input, conflicting flags, refused in agent mode
data.history-and-timeline#history and timelin:
apigent history "get-user" --json apigent timeline --since 24h --json An array, newest first:
[{"id":"e7770aa1-…","short_id":"e7770aa1","request":"get-user","time":"2026-10-20T18:41:41+05:30", "ok":true,"status":200,"duration_ms":0,"size_bytes":89}, {"id":"3baa2a2c-…","short_id":"3baa2a2c","request":"get-user","time":"…","ok":false, "duration_ms":0,"size_bytes":0,"error":"variable substitution failed: …","failure_phase":"request_build"}]
data.listing-and-inspecting#Listing and inspe: Command Shape apigent list --json Array of saved requests; literal credential headers and sensitive query params masked apigent show --json One saved request, masked the same way apigent env list --json [{"name","active","variables"}] (variables = count) apigent env show --json {"name","id","variables":{...},"secrets":[...]}, secrets masked apigent collection list --json [{"name","requests","variables","updated"}] (counts) apigent collection show --json {"name","id","variables":{...},"secrets":[...],"requests":[{"name","method","url"}]}, secrets masked apigent docs --json {"commands":[{"path","usage","args","flags":[...]}],"sections":{...}} --reveal (where supported) shows the masked values, and is refused in agent mode.
data.run#run:
apigent run --json prints one object per execution on stdout and nothing else: one line for a single run, NDJSON (one line per step or row) for --chain and --data. With --persist, persisted is on the last line.
Field Meaning id, short_id Execution record id; pass to apigent diag request, collection, environment, row What ran (row for --data iterations) ok No error, no failed assertion, and a 2xx status skipped, skip_reason The request was skipped (e.g. run-if) method, url The request as sent (secrets masked) status, status_text, duration_ms, size_bytes Response summary response_headers Object of header → value; sensitive headers masked body Parsed JSON when the body is valid JSON, otherwise a string error, failure_phase Why the attempt failed problems Resolution problems: [{"kind","variable","location","message"}] assertions [{"name","passed","message"}] extracted Values captured by --extract rules persisted {"environment","variables","collections":[{"name","variables"}]} Failure phases: request_build, http, extraction, assertion, status, pre_request_script, post_response_script, run_if, next_request.
Problem kinds: missing, leftover_placeholder, bad_type, unknown_dynamic, auth.
A request that could not be resolved:
{"id":"5a9eefb8-87bc-401d-94b7-b80c9a07cf18","short_id":"5a9eefb8","request":"get-user","ok":false, "method":"GET","url":"{{BASE}}/users?api_key={{API_KEY}}","duration_ms":0,"size_bytes":0, "error":"variable substitution failed: missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY","failure_phase":"request_build", "problems":[{"kind":"missing","variable":"BASE","location":"url","message":"missing required variable \"BASE\""}, {"kind":"missing","variable":"API_KEY","location":"header Authorization","message":"missing required variable \"API_KEY\""}]} A failed assertion:
{"ok":false,"status":200,"failure_phase":"assertion", "assertions":[{"name":"status = 201","passed":false,"message":"FAIL: status = 201 (actual: 200)"}], ...} Masking matches execution records (URL, request headers, errors, response headers). Outside agent mode the body is shown as received; in agent mode secrets are masked in the body too.
data.run---dry-run---json#run --dry-run --jso:
The planned request; nothing is sent or recorded. Exits 1 when problems is non-empty.
{"dry_run":true,"request":"get-user","environment":"dev","ok":true,"method":"GET", "url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****", "headers":[{"key":"Authorization","value":"*****"},{"key":"X-Merchant","value":"M-4242"}], "extracts":[{"name":"uid","source":"jsonpath:$.id"}]}

data: apigent mcp starts a Model Context Protocol server on stdin/stdout. Every saved request becomes a tool. Calls run in agent mode and return the same masked JSON as run --json.
data.set-up#Set up:
Store the secrets yourself, once:
apigent env create dev --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY apigent save get-user '{{BASE_URL}}/users/{{id}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}' Then add the server to your MCP client’s configuration:
{ "mcpServers": { "my-api": { "command": "apigent", "args": ["mcp", "--env", "dev"] } } } Flag Meaning --env, -e The environment every call runs against. Fixed for the server’s lifetime. Default: the active environment. --collection, -c Expose only the requests in this collection.
data.under-the-hood#Under the hood: Each call runs apigent --agent run --env --var ... in a child process. It gets exactly the CLI’s guarantees: one resolution path, masked output, an execution record you can inspect with apigent diag , and no way to reveal a secret. Calls are handled one at a time.
data.why-an-agent-cant-redirect-your-secrets#:
If a tool call could set any variable, an agent could pass BASE_URL=https://attacker.example. The request would then go out with your Authorization header to a host the agent controls. apigent refuses any argument that the environment or collection already defines, and nothing is sent:
argument "BASE_URL" is not allowed: only placeholders the environment leaves undefined can be set (allowed: id) So define every host in the environment or collection, never leave it as a placeholder for the agent to fill.

data: Everything that enters an LLM context window may be stored, logged, or reused in ways you don’t control. If a credential touches a context window, treat it as exposed. apigent’s job is to make sure the agent never needs to see one.
data.before-and-after#Before and after: # Before: the key is in the command, the shell history and the agent's context curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123def456" https://api.example.com/users # After: set up once by a human apigent env create prod --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY apigent save "get-users" '{{BASE_URL}}/users' --auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' # The agent runs agentapigent run "get-users" --env prod
data.limits#Limits: A secret has to be known to apigent to be masked: marked secret, sensitively named, or written into a credential header, sensitive query parameter or auth param. An unrelated value in a response body that happens to be sensitive is not masked. Values shorter than 4 characters are not replaced inside free text. Outside agent mode, run prints response bodies as received. Give agents agentapigent, not apigent.
data.the-layers#The layers:
1. Requests are referenced by name. The agent runs agentapigent run "get-users" --env prod. The command contains a request name and an environment name, never a value.
2. Secrets are encrypted at rest. Environment and collection secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and decrypted only at send time. See Credential storage.
3. Auth is applied by apigent. Saved auth configs (--auth bearer --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}') are filled and applied to the outgoing request inside apigent.
4. Everything apigent shows or stores is masked. show, list --json, codegen, paste, env show, dry runs, run --json URLs/headers/errors and execution records replace secret values with *****, including URL- and JSON-escaped copies. See Secret masking.
5. Agent mode masks the rest. With --agent, secrets are also masked in response bodies, response headers, errors and apigent exec child output; --reveal, paste, codegen --clipboard and run --output are refused.
$ agentapigent env show prod {"name":"prod","variables":{"API_KEY":"*****","BASE_URL":"https://api.example.com"},"secrets":["API_KEY"], ...} $ agentapigent run "whoami" --env prod {"ok":true,"status":200,"body":{"token_echo":"*****"}, ...} 6. Failures are diagnosable without secrets. Execution records never contain secret values, so apigent diag can show the agent what changed since the last success, comparing secret variables by origin only.
data.the-risks#The risks: Context exposure. A key pasted into a prompt, or printed by a command the agent ran, stays in the conversation. History and logs. Conversations and tool output are often retained. Accidental output. Models repeat what they’ve seen, for example in generated code or debugging output. Echoed secrets. APIs often echo credentials back: in a redirect URL, an error message, a debug field of the response body.

data:
For contributors and plugin authors. You don’t need this page to use apigent.
apigent CLI is a Go binary designed for single-file distribution. The architecture follows a layered approach where each layer depends only on the layers below it.
data.9-layer-architecture#9-Layer Architectur: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CLI (urfave/cli) │ │ save run list edit delete env collection codegen... │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Core Services │ │ Template Engine │ Auth Registry │ Formatter │ │ Curl Parser │ Scripting │ Assertions │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Storage (goleveldb) │ │ Requests │ Collections │ Environments │ History │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ HTTP Client (net/http) │ │ TLS │ Timeouts │ Proxies │ Cookie Jar │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Protocol Handlers │ │ HTTP │ GraphQL │ gRPC │ WebSocket │ SSE │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Plugin System │ │ Middleware │ Output │ Command │ Auth │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ TUI (bubbletea) — not functional │ │ Sidebar │ Request Builder │ Response Viewer │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
data.data-storage#Data Storage:
apigent stores data in two locations:
Location Path Purpose Database ~/.local/share/apigent/apigent.db Requests, collections, environments, history Config ~/.config/apigent/config.toml User preferences, plugin settings The database uses goleveldb (LevelDB port) for high-performance key-value storage. Configuration uses TOML for human-readable settings.
data.layer-descriptions#Layer Descriptions:
CLI Layer - Uses urfave/cli for command-line argument parsing. Handles all user-facing commands like apigent save, apigent run, and apigent edit.
Core Services Layer - Contains the business logic. Request resolution (internal/resolve) turns a saved request plus its scopes into the request to send, or into the list of resolution problems; it is shared by run, collection run, the shell and the TUI. Masking rules (internal/redact) are shared by every command that shows or stores a request, and by execution records. Auth registry manages API keys, Bearer tokens, and basic auth. Formatter provides response rendering in multiple formats.
Storage Layer - goleveldb-backed persistence for requests, collections, environments, and execution history. Provides ACID-like transactions for data integrity.
HTTP Client Layer - Wraps Go’s net/http with TLS configuration, timeout handling, proxy support, and cookie jar management.
Protocol Handlers Layer - Extends beyond HTTP to support GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, and Server-Sent Events. Each handler translates between protocol-specific formats and apigent’s internal request/response model.
Plugin System Layer - Four plugin types: MiddlewarePlugin runs before/after requests, OutputPlugin formats responses, CommandPlugin adds new CLI commands, and AuthPlugin provides custom authentication handlers (added in v0.3.0). All plugins are discovered from ~/.config/apigent/plugins/.
TUI Layer - Built with bubbletea. The code exists but is not functional in the current release. The intended design is a full-screen three-pane workspace for browsing requests, editing them, and inspecting responses.
data.request-lifecycle#Request Lifecycle: CLI parses command and loads request from storage Pre-request scripting executes (JavaScript/goja) Request resolution fills placeholders from the scopes (environment < collection < data row < CLI < runtime) and applies auth; any problem stops the request here Middleware plugins run their ApplyBeforeRequest hooks Protocol handler sends the request Middleware plugins run their ApplyAfterResponse hooks Post-response scripting executes Assertions are evaluated Output plugin formats and displays the response The execution is recorded, with secrets masked, whether it succeeded or failed at any earlier step (inspect with apigent diag)

data: apigent’s plugin system lets you extend functionality through middleware, output, command, and auth plugin interfaces. Go plugins are discovered from ~/.config/apigent/plugins/ and loaded into the plugin registry on startup.
data.authplugin#AuthPlugin:
Applies authentication to an outgoing request. Auth plugins expose parameter metadata through the same auth.ParamDef shape used by built-in handlers.
type AuthPlugin interface { Name() string Params() []auth.ParamDef Apply(req *client.Request, params map[string]string) error }
data.built-in-output-plugins#Built-in Output:
Plugin Description Example Output pretty Formatted JSON/XML with syntax highlighting Colored, indented output slack Slack-compatible attachment format Block kit payload markdown Markdown code blocks json ... csv Tabular data extraction Comma-separated values minimal Single-line summary 200 OK - 123ms - 2.1KB Select an output plugin with the --format flag:
apigent run "api" --format slack
data.commandplugin#CommandPlugin:
Adds new CLI commands. Use for project-specific workflows or integrations.
type CommandPlugin interface { Name() string Command() string Description() string Run(args []string) error }
data.creating-a-custom-plugin#Creating a Cust:
Custom plugins are currently low-level Go plugins, not a polished external SDK. A plugin must export a Plugin symbol whose value implements at least one known plugin interface. This example imports apigent’s internal/... packages, so build it under the apigent module tree or another module path that Go permits to import those internal packages.
Minimal middleware plugin:
package main import ( "github.com/bsreeram08/apigent/internal/client" "github.com/bsreeram08/apigent/internal/plugins" ) type HeaderPlugin struct{} func (HeaderPlugin) Name() string { return "example-header" } func (HeaderPlugin) BeforeRequest(ctx *plugins.RequestContext) *plugins.RequestContext { if ctx != nil && ctx.Request != nil { ctx.Request.Headers = append(ctx.Request.Headers, client.Header{ Key: "X-apigent-Plugin", Value: "example-header", }) } return ctx } func (HeaderPlugin) AfterResponse(ctx *plugins.ResponseContext) *plugins.ResponseContext { return ctx } var Plugin = HeaderPlugin{} Build and place the shared object where the loader expects it:
mkdir -p ~/.config/apigent/plugins/example-header go build -buildmode=plugin -o ~/.config/apigent/plugins/example-header/example-header.so ./plugin.go The loader discovers enabled plugins at ~/.config/apigent/plugins//.so, looks up the exported Plugin symbol, and accepts values that implement MiddlewarePlugin, OutputPlugin, CommandPlugin, or AuthPlugin.
data.current-support#Current support:
The registry and loader can categorize values that implement MiddlewarePlugin, OutputPlugin, CommandPlugin, or AuthPlugin. Auth plugins are stored separately from middleware and can be listed or looked up through the registry.
External plugin packaging is still low-level Go plugin support. The loader expects plugins under ~/.config/apigent/plugins//.so and a Plugin symbol that implements at least one known plugin interface. Go plugin loading is only supported on Linux amd64 and Linux arm64.
data.middlewareplugin#MiddlewarePlugin:
Runs before and after each request. Use for logging, timing, retry logic, and request modification.
type MiddlewarePlugin interface { Name() string BeforeRequest(ctx *RequestContext) *RequestContext AfterResponse(ctx *ResponseContext) *ResponseContext }
data.outputplugin#OutputPlugin:
Formats and displays responses. apigent includes built-in output plugins, but custom plugins can provide specialized formatting.
type OutputPlugin interface { Name() string Format() string Render(ctx *ResponseContext) string }
data.plugin-discovery#Plugin Discovery:
On startup, apigent discovers shared objects at ~/.config/apigent/plugins//.so. If an enabled-plugin list is configured, only matching names are loaded. Each plugin file must export a Plugin symbol:
// plugin.go package main import "github.com/bsreeram08/apigent/..." var Plugin = MyMiddlewarePlugin{}
data.plugin-registry#Plugin Registry:
The registry stores each plugin by the interfaces it implements.
type Registry struct { middleware []MiddlewarePlugin outputs []OutputPlugin commands []CommandPlugin auths []AuthPlugin } func (r *Registry) Register(plugin interface{}) { switch p := plugin.(type) { case MiddlewarePlugin: r.middleware = append(r.middleware, p) case OutputPlugin: r.outputs = append(r.outputs, p) case CommandPlugin: r.commands = append(r.commands, p) case AuthPlugin: r.auths = append(r.auths, p) } } Auth plugins are stored separately from middleware and can be listed or looked up by name before their Apply method updates a request.
data.request-execution-touchpoints#Request ex:
During a request run, extensions can affect different parts of execution:
Middleware plugins - Can inspect or change request context before the request and response context after the response Auth handlers - Apply saved auth settings after templates are substituted and before the request is sent Output plugins - Render the response when their format is selected Custom middleware inserts into this chain via the registry.
data.security#Security:
Plugins run with the user’s permissions. apigent applies these safeguards:
If an enabled list is configured, plugins not on that list are skipped Middleware BeforeRequest and AfterResponse calls are wrapped in panic recovery Plugin discovery treats a missing plugin directory as empty Individual plugin load failures print a warning to stderr and do not stop other plugins from loading

data: One page per command, in alphabetical order. Every page has the same layout: synopsis, flags, aliases, examples and related commands. Flag tables are checked against apigent docs --json from the binary; run apigent docs for the reference that matches your installed version.
data.commands#Commands: Command What it does auth List auth handlers and their parameters codegen Generate Go, Python, JavaScript or curl code from a request collection Manage collections, their variables, and collection runs cookies List, delete and clear stored cookies delete Remove a saved request detect Parse a curl command from stdin or a file diag Inspect one recorded execution diff Compare the latest responses of a request docs Print a compact reference of every command and concept edit Change fields of a saved request env Manage environments and their variables exec Run a command with an environment’s variables injected export Export requests to a file extract Test extraction rules against a sample response graphql Execute a GraphQL query grpc Execute a gRPC request history Show execution history for a request import Import from OpenAPI, Insomnia, Bruno, Postman, HAR or apigent exports init Initialize a project (.apigent/) list List saved requests paste Copy a request as curl to the clipboard receive Decrypt a share bundle and import it rename Rename a saved request run Execute a saved request save Save a request under a name sequence Set execution order within a collection share Encrypt requests to a recipient’s public key shell Launch the typed interactive shell show Show a saved request sse Connect to a Server-Sent Events endpoint timeline Show executions across all requests update Update apigent to the latest release ws Open a WebSocket connection apigent tui is a hidden, non-functional stub; use apigent shell for interactive use.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error; apigent exec exits with its command’s code. Details and the JSON error shape are in JSON output.
data.global-flags#Global flags:
These work with every command, in any position.
Flag Short Description --agent JSON output, no prompts, strict masking (or APIGENT_AGENT=1, or run the binary as agentapigent). See Agent mode. --no-input Never prompt; fail and name what to pass instead (or APIGENT_NO_INPUT=1) --project-dir Project root containing .apigent (or legacy .gurl) file storage (or APIGENT_PROJECT_DIR) --version -v Print the version

data: List the built-in auth handlers and the parameters each one accepts, so you know what to pass to --auth and --auth-param on apigent save and apigent edit.
data.info#info:
Show the parameters for one auth type, marked required/optional and secret, with defaults.
apigent auth info None.
data.list#list:
List the built-in auth types.
apigent auth list None.
data.oauth-2-client-credentials#OAuth 2 clien: apigent save "service-token" https://api.example.com/service \ --auth oauth2 \ --auth-param flow=client_credentials \ --auth-param client_id='{{client_id}}' \ --auth-param client_secret='{{client_secret}}' \ --auth-param token_url='https://auth.example.com/oauth/token' \ --auth-param scope='read:orders' To change or clear saved auth, use apigent edit --auth ... or apigent edit --auth none.
data.related-commands#Related commands: apigent save - Save auth with a request apigent edit - Update or clear saved auth apigent run - Execute a request with saved auth Credential storage - Where auth params are stored
data.save-bearer-auth-that-reads-a-secret-fro: apigent save "profile" '{{BASE_URL}}/me' \ --auth bearer \ --auth-param token='{{API_KEY}}' apigent run "profile" --env prod
data.see-what-a-handler-needs#See what a hand: apigent auth info bearer Auth type: bearer Parameters: token	required,secret	Bearer token value
data.synopsis#Synopsis:
apigent auth list apigent auth info apigent run applies the auth saved on the request. Auth params may contain placeholders (token='{{API_KEY}}'); they are filled during request resolution, then the handler updates the outgoing request. Literal secret auth params are masked by show, list --json, codegen and paste.
Type Use it for basic HTTP Basic auth with username and password bearer Bearer tokens in the Authorization header apikey API key in a header or query parameter oauth1 OAuth 1.0 signed requests oauth2 OAuth 2.0 auth_code or client credentials flow awsv4 AWS SigV4 request signing digest Digest Authorization headers from supplied challenge values ntlm NTLM negotiate or challenge response headers

data: Turn a saved request into Go, Python, JavaScript or curl code. Literal secrets are masked by default.
data.flags#Flags: Flag Short Default Description --lang -l none Language to generate: go, python, javascript, curl --clipboard -c false Copy the output to the clipboard instead of printing it --reveal false Include secret header and auth values instead of masking them (Authorization always becomes a placeholder)
data.related-commands#Related commands: apigent paste - Copy a request as curl apigent show - Show a saved request apigent export - Export requests to a file
data.synopsis#Synopsis:
apigent codegen --lang |python|javascript|curl> [flags] Literal secret header values, sensitive query parameters and secret auth params are masked as *****. data.synopsis#Synopsis:
apigent diag [flags] apigent diag --id [flags] Every execution of run (single requests, --chain steps and --data rows), collection run and shell send is recorded, including failures before a response: resolution problems, connection errors and timeouts, script errors, assertion failures and non-2xx responses. Dry runs are not recorded.
A failed run prints the record id on stderr:
request failed: HTTP 500 (id: 7e0d3985) — inspect with: apigent diag 7e0d3985 collection run prints the id next to each failed request, apigent history lists ids, and run --json includes id and short_id in the JSON object. Any unique prefix of an id works.
diag prints:
Summary: request, id, time, environment, result, status, failure phase, duration and size Request: method, URL, headers and body as sent Variables: each variable with its variable origin (environment, collection, data row, CLI, runtime) and value; secrets show as ***** Response: status, headers and body (the first 4KB unless --full) Assertions: each result Compared with last success: status, duration, URL, headers and body, variable values and origins, response headers and top-level JSON fields that changed Records never contain secrets: secret and credential-looking values are masked before saving, so secret variables are compared by origin only. Response bodies are stored as received. In agent mode, diag also masks secrets in the response body and headers, using the secrets of both compared runs.

data.flags#Flags: Flag Short Default Description --identity -i see Keys Private key to decrypt with (repeatable) --dry-run false Show the bundle’s contents without importing --yes -y false Import without asking (required when reading from stdin or with --no-input) --force -f false Overwrite existing requests and collections with the same name --require-signed false Refuse bundles whose sender isn’t verified against GitHub --update-keys false Accept and re-pin the sender’s changed GitHub keys
data.keys#Keys: receive tries, in order: each --identity, $APIGENT_SHARE_IDENTITY, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 and ~/.ssh/id_rsa. ed25519 and RSA SSH keys and age identity files (AGE-SECRET-KEY-...) work. A passphrase-protected key prompts for its passphrase; ssh-agent can’t be used, because decryption needs the private key itself.

data.related-commands#Related commands: apigent share - Encrypt requests for someone apigent import - Import unencrypted exports and other formats
data.synopsis#Synopsis: apigent receive |-> [--identity ...] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--force] [--require-signed] Pass - to read the bundle from stdin. Armored and binary bundles are both accepted.
data.what-gets-imported#What gets imported: Before importing, receive prints the collection, each request’s method, name and URL (marking pre/post scripts and auth), and whether secrets are included, then asks to confirm. Nothing runs on receive, but a request’s scripts run when you later run it, so check them with apigent show first. Requests are matched to local ones by name only: the sender’s internal IDs are dropped, and a loose request (not part of a shared collection) is imported without a collection, so it can’t join one of yours and read its secrets. Existing requests and collections are kept unless you pass --force. Imported secret values are encrypted at rest with your local key, like any other collection secret.
data.who-sent-it#Who sent it:
The preview ends with the sender check:
Line Meaning ✓ Signed by github:bob (SHA256:...) The signature is valid and the key is one GitHub publishes for bob Signed by key SHA256:... The signature is valid; the sender didn’t claim a GitHub account Signed by key SHA256:..., claims github:bob (couldn't check: ...) Valid signature, but GitHub couldn’t be reached or bob’s keys changed since they were pinned ⚠ Unsigned: the sender can't be verified No signature A broken signature, or a bundle that claims github:bob but is signed by a key that isn’t bob’s, is refused outright. --require-signed also refuses anything that isn’t verified against GitHub. Sender keys are pinned in ~/.config/apigent/known_keys.json the same way share pins recipients; --update-keys accepts a changed set.

data: Execute a previously saved request by name.
data.execution-records-and-the-failure-notice:
Every execution is recorded, including attempts that never got a response (resolution problems, connection errors, timeouts, script errors), assertion failures and non-2xx responses. Dry runs are not recorded. When a run fails, apigent names the record on stderr:
request failed: HTTP 500 (id: bbd47546) — inspect with: apigent diag bbd47546 Pass that id to apigent diag. Execution records never contain secrets; see Header Redaction.
data.exit-codes#Exit codes: Code Meaning 0 Success. A non-2xx response is still 0 unless --fail is passed. 1 Request or environment not found, resolution problems, transport error, script or extraction error, failed assertion, non-2xx with --fail, dry run with problems 2 Usage: missing request name with --no-input, conflicting flags (--persist --dry-run), --reveal or --output in agent mode
data.fail-on-non-2xx-responses#Fail on non-2x: apigent run "create-order" --env prod --fail | jq . By default a non-2xx response still exits 0. With --fail it exits 1; the body is still printed to stdout.
data.flags#Flags: Flag Short Default Description --env -e none Environment to use for variable substitution. An unknown environment is an error. --var -v none Variable as key=value (repeatable). Highest scope except runtime values. --format -f auto Output format: auto, json, or table --output -o none Write the response to a file (- for stdout). Refused in agent mode. --force false Overwrite the output file if it exists --timeout none Request timeout (e.g., 5s, 1m, 30s) --chain --ch false Enable request chaining via setNextRequest --persist false Write extracted and script-set variables back to their variable origin --dry-run false Resolve the request and print it without sending it --assert -a none Assertion to evaluate (repeatable), e.g. status=200 --fail false Exit non-zero when the response status is not 2xx (the body is still printed) --data -d none CSV or JSON data file for data-driven iteration --json -j false One JSON object per execution (NDJSON for --chain/--data), nothing else on stdout --persist and --dry-run cannot be used together (exit code 2).
data.machine-readable-output#Machine-readable:
apigent run "get-user" --env dev --json stdout gets one JSON object per execution (one line). Empty fields are omitted:
{"id":"50488e65-9cb3-4cbe-a5b2-769258964b6e","short_id":"50488e65","request":"get-user","environment":"dev", "ok":true,"method":"GET","url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****","status":200,"status_text":"OK", "duration_ms":4,"size_bytes":89,"response_headers":{"Content-Type":"application/json","Set-Cookie":"*****"}, "body":{"id":"u-123"},"extracted":{"uid":"u-123"}} (Wrapped here for reading; the real output is one line.)
The full set of fields is:
id short_id request collection environment row ok skipped skip_reason method url status status_text duration_ms size_bytes response_headers body error failure_phase problems[{kind,variable,location,message}] assertions[{name,passed,message}] extracted persisted{environment,variables,collections[{name,variables}]} ok is true when there was no error, no failed assertion and the status was 2xx. body is the parsed JSON value when the body is valid JSON, otherwise a string. A failed attempt has error and failure_phase: request_build, http, extraction, assertion, status, pre_request_script, post_response_script, run_if or next_request. Requests that cannot be resolved list structured problems. Problem kinds are missing, leftover_placeholder, bad_type, unknown_dynamic and auth: {"ok":false,"failure_phase":"request_build","error":"variable substitution failed: missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY", "problems":[{"kind":"missing","variable":"BASE","location":"url","message":"missing required variable \"BASE\""}, ...]} --chain steps and --data rows each print one line (NDJSON). With --persist, persisted is on the last line. Masking matches execution records: secret values are masked in the URL, request data, response headers and errors. The body is shown as received, except in agent mode, where secrets are masked in the body too. The failure notice is not printed with --json; the record id is in the object (id, short_id). With --json, errors before any execution (unknown request or environment, conflicting flags) print {"ok":false,"error":"..."} on stdout, as well as the message on stderr. --dry-run --json prints the planned request instead:
{"dry_run":true,"request":"get-user","environment":"dev","ok":true,"method":"GET", "url":"http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=*****", "headers":[{"key":"Authorization","value":"*****"},{"key":"X-Merchant","value":"M-4242"}], "extracts":[{"name":"uid","source":"jsonpath:$.id"}]}
data.output-streams#Output streams: The response body goes to stdout. Status lines, notes (for example note: uid not saved; add --persist to use them in later runs), persist summaries, assertion summaries and Response saved go to stderr, so apigent run ... | jq . sees only the body. With --json, stdout carries only JSON (see below).
data.persist-flow-variables#Persist flow vari:
apigent run "login" --chain --persist --env staging Without --persist, extracted and script-set variables are dropped at the end of the run and run prints a note naming them. With --persist, each one is written back to its variable origin: values that came from the environment go to the environment (--env or the active one), others to the request’s collection, otherwise to the environment. CLI variables and data-row values are not written back unless extraction or a script changes them.
--persist refuses to write a value that contains {{ (for example refusing to persist "tpl": value contains "{{"), and returns an error for a locked collection instead of overwriting it.
data.preview-without-sending-dry-run#Preview: apigent run "get-user" --env dev --dry-run GET http://127.0.0.1:18731/users?api_key=***** Authorization: ***** X-Merchant: M-4242 extract: uid <- jsonpath:$.id The dry run shows the request after pre-request scripts run, with secrets masked. It never applies auth (applying auth could contact a token endpoint), leaves {{$uuid}}-style dynamic functions in place, sends nothing, records nothing, and exits 1 when the request has resolution problems.
data.related-commands#Related commands: apigent diag - Inspect a recorded execution apigent save - Save a new request apigent extract - Test extraction rules offline apigent history - View execution history apigent env - Manage environments Agent mode - JSON output and strict masking for AI agents
data.run-a-chained-request#Run a chained requ: apigent run "login" --chain --env staging Enables request chaining for saved post-response scripts that call apigent.setNextRequest(...). Extracted variables and variables set by scripts become available to later requests in the chain.
data.run-a-request-with-saved-auth#Run a requ: apigent save "profile" https://api.example.com/me \ --auth bearer \ --auth-param token='{{token}}' apigent run "profile" --var token=abc123 The saved bearer auth handler adds the Authorization: Bearer abc123 header during execution. You don’t need to resupply --auth when running the request.
data.synopsis#Synopsis:
apigent run [flags] The run command executes a request that was previously saved with apigent save. You can pick an environment, override variables, set timeouts, validate responses with assertions, iterate over a data file, and follow request chains.
Before anything is sent, apigent performs request resolution: every {{placeholder}} in the URL, headers, body and auth params is filled from the scopes (environment < collection < data row < CLI --var < runtime). If any placeholder cannot be filled, the request is not sent and every resolution problem is reported at once, for example missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY. See Environments and variables for the placeholder rules.
If the saved request has auth settings, apigent run applies them after the placeholders are filled.

data: Encrypt one request, one collection or every request to another person’s public key. Only that person’s private key can open the result, so the file is safe to send over Slack, email or a gist. The recipient imports it with apigent receive.
data.flags#Flags: Flag Short Default Description --name -n none Share one request by name (or pass it as the argument) --collection -c none Share an entire collection with its variables --all -a false Share all requests --to none Recipient (repeatable, required) --output -o stdout Output file, written with mode 0600 --with-secrets false Include secret collection variable values (requires --collection) --binary false Write raw age output instead of ASCII armor --sign see Signing SSH private key to sign with --no-sign false Send the bundle unsigned --from $APIGENT_SHARE_FROM Who you are, e.g. github:; checked by the receiver --update-keys false Accept and re-pin a recipient’s changed GitHub keys
data.how-it-works#How it works: The bundle is the same JSON that apigent export writes, plus a kind: gurl-share marker, encrypted with age (filippo.io/age). Any standard age CLI can decrypt it with the recipient’s key. A signed bundle wraps that JSON with an SSHSIG signature over its exact bytes before encryption, so the sender’s identity is visible only to the recipient.
data.key-pinning#Key pinning: The first time you share with github:, apigent records the fingerprints of their keys in ~/.config/apigent/known_keys.json. If the set changes later (a new laptop, or a taken-over account), share stops and lists the added and removed keys. Re-run with --update-keys once you’ve confirmed the change with the person.
data.recipients#Recipients: --to value Resolved by github: The public SSH keys GitHub publishes at https://github.com/.keys a file path A .pub or authorized_keys-style file, one key per line ssh-ed25519 AAAA... / ssh-rsa AAAA... The literal public key age1... A native age X25519 recipient The bundle is encrypted to every usable key of every recipient, so any of their machines can open it. ecdsa and security-key (sk-) SSH keys can’t be used for encryption; they are skipped with a warning. Each recipient key’s fingerprint is printed to stderr so you can check it.
data.related-commands#Related commands: apigent receive - Decrypt and import a share bundle apigent export - Unencrypted export, or passphrase-protected collection secrets
data.secrets#Secrets: Secret collection variables are sent with an empty value and keep their secret flag; the recipient fills in their own. --with-secrets includes the values, protected by the bundle’s encryption. Request headers, bodies and auth params are sent as stored: a literal value under a sensitive header such as Authorization is shared as-is, and share warns about it. Use {{variables}} to keep tokens out of shared requests.
data.send-one-request-to-a-github-user#Send o: apigent share get-user --to github:alice --from github:bob The ASCII-armored output can be pasted straight into a chat message.
data.share-a-collection-with-two-people#Share: apigent share -c payments-api --to github:alice --to github:bob -o payments.gurl.age
data.signing#Signing:
Bundles are signed with your SSH key so the receiver can tell who sent them. share signs with --sign , else $APIGENT_SHARE_IDENTITY, else ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 or ~/.ssh/id_rsa. If none of the default keys can be used, the bundle goes out unsigned with a warning; --no-sign skips signing on purpose.
Pass --from github: (or set APIGENT_SHARE_FROM) and the receiver checks that the signing key is one of the keys GitHub publishes for you. Signatures use OpenSSH’s SSHSIG format with the namespace gurl-share, so ssh-keygen -Y verify can check them too.

data:
Install apigent, then follow the quickstart: save a request, run it, move its values into an environment, and group requests in a collection.
Installation — Homebrew, install script, container image, binaries, or source. Quickstart — save → run → environment → collection.
apigent ships as a single static binary with no runtime dependencies. Pick one install method, then verify and continue to the Quickstart.
data.install#Install:
HomebrewScriptBinaryDockerSource macOS and Linux:
brew tap bsreeram08/apigent https://github.com/bsreeram08/apigent brew install apigent curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bsreeram08/apigent/master/scripts/install.sh | bash Detects your platform, downloads the matching binary from the latest release , and installs it to /usr/local/bin.
Download from GitHub Releases :
# macOS (Apple Silicon) curl -LO https://github.com/bsreeram08/apigent/releases/latest/download/apigent-darwin-arm64.tar.gz tar -xzf apigent-darwin-arm64.tar.gz && sudo mv apigent /usr/local/bin/apigent # Linux (x86_64) curl -LO https://github.com/bsreeram08/apigent/releases/latest/download/apigent-linux-amd64.tar.gz tar -xzf apigent-linux-amd64.tar.gz && sudo mv apigent /usr/local/bin/apigent # Linux (ARM64) curl -LO https://github.com/bsreeram08/apigent/releases/latest/download/apigent-linux-arm64.tar.gz tar -xzf apigent-linux-arm64.tar.gz && sudo mv apigent /usr/local/bin/apigent Each release also includes raw binaries and SHA256SUMS.
Every release tag publishes a multi-arch image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) to GitHub Container Registry: ghcr.io/bsreeram08/apigent:latest (newest stable release; pre-releases don’t move it) and one tag per release, matching the GitHub release tag, e.g. v0.7.0.
docker run --rm ghcr.io/bsreeram08/apigent:latest --version docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/bsreeram08/apigent:latest list docker run --rm ghcr.io/bsreeram08/apigent:v0.7.0 --version # pinned, reproducible Keep the database, project files and key material across runs by mounting the host directories:
docker run --rm \ -v "$PWD:/work" \ -v "$HOME/.local/share/apigent:/home/apigent/.local/share/apigent" \ -v "$HOME/.config/apigent:/home/apigent/.config/apigent" \ -w /work \ ghcr.io/bsreeram08/apigent:latest list The package is public. If GitHub still shows it as private, log in with a token that has read:packages: echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$GITHUB_USER" --password-stdin.
Requires Go 1.25.0+.
git clone https://github.com/bsreeram08/apigent.git cd apigent go build -o apigent ./cmd/apigent sudo mv apigent /usr/local/bin/apigent
