data.move-values-into-an-environment#Move val:
Hard-coded hosts and tokens don’t belong in saved requests. Use {{placeholders}} and put the values in an environment:
apigent env create dev \ --var BASE_URL=https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com \ --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY # KEY=- reads the value from stdin, without echo apigent save "get-user" '{{BASE_URL}}/users/{{id}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}' apigent run "get-user" --env dev --var id=1 Secret values are encrypted at rest and shown as ***** by apigent env show dev. If a placeholder can’t be filled, apigent refuses to send the request and names every missing variable. See Variables & placeholders.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Environments & secrets and Variables & placeholders Chaining & extraction — log in once, reuse the token Agent mode — let an AI agent run your requests without seeing secrets CLI reference — every command and flag
data.run-it#Run it:
apigent run "list-users" The response body goes to stdout; status lines and notes go to stderr, so piping works:
apigent run "list-users" | jq '.[0].email' Add assertions, or make non-2xx responses fail the command:
apigent run "list-users" --assert "status=200" --fail
data.save-a-request#Save a request:
apigent save "list-users" https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users A saved request has a name, a method, a URL, and optional headers, body, auth and extraction rules. You can also paste a curl command:
apigent save "create-user" --curl "curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"name\":\"Ada\"}' https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users" Check what you saved:
apigent list apigent show "create-user"

data:
Each guide covers one task end to end. Read them in order the first time; later, jump to the one you need.
Guide Read it when you want to… Environments & secrets keep hosts and credentials out of saved requests, switch dev/staging/prod Variables & placeholders understand {{placeholders}}, typed and dynamic values, scope precedence, --persist Chaining & extraction pull a token or id out of one response and use it in the next request Collections & data-driven runs run a group of requests in order, feed CSV/JSON rows, produce CI reports Diagnosing failures find out why a run failed and what changed since it last worked Scripting & assertions check responses, or run JavaScript before and after a request Other protocols call GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket or SSE endpoints
Extraction rules capture values from a response; chaining runs the next request with those values. Together they turn “log in, then call the API with the token” into one command.
data.1-write-and-test-an-extraction-rule#1. W:
A rule has the form VAR=METHOD:EXPR:
Method Captures Example jsonpath A JSONPath value (array indexes supported) orderId=jsonpath:$.data.items[0].id jq Alias of jsonpath token=jq:$.token header A response header location=header:Location regex The first capture group n=regex:"amount":(\d+) Test it against a sample response first. No request is sent:
echo '{"token":"t-123","user":{"id":42}}' | apigent extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' 'uid=jsonpath:$.user.id' token = t-123 uid = 42 See apigent extract.
data.2-save-the-rule-on-the-request#2. Save t:
apigent save "login" '{{BASE_URL}}/auth/login' -X POST \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"user":"{{USER}}","password":"{{PASSWORD}}"}' \ --extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' # or add it to an existing request apigent edit "login" --extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' Run it with --json to see what was extracted:
apigent run "login" --env dev --json | jq .extracted
data.3-chain-to-the-next-request#3. Chain to:
A post-response script picks the next request with apigent.setNextRequest. Run the first request with --chain:
apigent edit "login" --post-script 'apigent.setNextRequest("profile")' apigent save "profile" '{{BASE_URL}}/me' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{token}}' apigent run "login" --env dev --chain Extracted and script-set values are runtime values: the highest scope, available to every later request, assertion, script and run-if check in the same run. With --json, each step prints one line (NDJSON).
Skip a step conditionally with a saved run-if expression (VAR == VALUE or VAR != VALUE; missing variables count as empty):
apigent edit "profile" --run-if "token != ''"
Runtime values are dropped at the end of the run, and run prints a note naming them. Add --persist to write them back to their variable origin:
apigent run "login" --env dev --chain --persist --persist refuses values that contain {{ and locked collections. Details: Variables & placeholders.
data.see-also#See also: Collections & data-driven runs — chains across a whole collection Scripting & assertions — the script API

data: A collection groups saved requests and carries its own variables and secrets. apigent collection run executes its requests in order, once per iteration or data row, and reports pass/fail for each.
data.build-a-collection#Build a collection: apigent collection create "checkout" --var CURRENCY=EUR --secret API_KEY=sk-test-... apigent save "create-order" '{{BASE_URL}}/orders' -X POST -c checkout \ --extract 'orderId=jsonpath:$.id' apigent save "capture-payment" '{{BASE_URL}}/orders/{{orderId}}/capture' -X POST -c checkout apigent collection show "checkout" # requests and variables (secrets masked) Collection variables sit between environment and data-row values in scope precedence, and may reference environment keys (API_URL={{BASE_URL}}/v1).
data.data-driven-runs#Data-driven runs:
Feed rows from CSV or JSON; each row is one iteration, and its columns become data-row variables:
email,name alice@example.com,Alice bob@example.com,Bob apigent collection run "signup" --data users.csv --env staging apigent run "create-user" --data users.json # a single request works too JSON data is an array of objects: [{"email": "alice@example.com", "name": "Alice"}].
Repeat without data using --iterations 3, and pace requests with --delay 200ms.
data.file-backed-reloads#File-backed reloads: For project-backed collections (apigent init, apigent collection migrate), a long collection run watches the collection files. The current iteration always uses the snapshot it started with; changes (debounced) apply from the next iteration or data row.
data.flow-variables-across-requests#Flow vari:
Extraction rules and scripts share one map of runtime values. A value extracted by one request is available to later requests’ placeholders, assertions, scripts and run-if checks:
apigent edit "create-order" --post-script "apigent.setNextRequest('capture-payment')" apigent edit "capture-payment" --run-if "orderId != ''" Write them back to their variable origin at the end of the run with --persist (not combinable with --dry-run):
apigent collection run "checkout" --env staging --persist Assertions can use those values too, and a request that asserts its status may expect an error:
apigent save "read-order" '{{BASE_URL}}/orders/{{orderId}}' -c checkout apigent edit "read-order" -a 'status=200' -a 'body.data.id={{orderId}}' apigent save "locked-account" '{{BASE_URL}}/billing' -c checkout apigent edit "locked-account" -a 'status=402' -a 'body.errorCodes[0]=ACCESS_ENDED' Without a status assertion, any non-2xx response fails the request.
See Chaining & extraction.
data.preview-then-run#Preview, then run:
apigent collection run "checkout" --env staging --dry-run apigent collection run "checkout" --env staging A dry run prints the request order and each resolved request without sending anything, running post-response scripts, recording history, writing reports or persisting variables.
A failed request prints its execution id on stderr, ready for apigent diag:
[FAIL] capture-payment: HTTP 500 (id: 01dda65f) — inspect with: apigent diag 01dda65f apigent collection run exits 1 when any request fails.
data.reports-for-ci#Reports for CI:
Reporters are console, junit, json and html; repeat --reporter for several. Files go to --reporter-output DIR (as report.xml, report.json, …). Create the directory first:
mkdir -p reports apigent collection run "api-tests" --env ci --reporter junit --reporter json --reporter-output reports --ci # GitHub Actions - name: Run API tests run: | mkdir -p reports apigent collection run "api-tests" --env ci --reporter junit --reporter-output reports --bail - name: Publish test results uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1 with: name: API tests path: reports/report.xml reporter: java-junit Add --verbose to print request and response headers and bodies for each request.
data.see-also#See also: apigent collection — every subcommand and flag, including sharing collections through git with passphrase-encrypted secrets apigent sequence
data.set-the-order#Set the order: apigent sequence set "create-order" 1 apigent sequence set "capture-payment" 2 apigent sequence list "checkout"
data.stop-early#Stop early: Flag Effect --bail Stop on the first failure of any kind; remaining requests are skipped --assert-bail Stop on the first failed assertion only --ci CI mode: treat skipped requests as failures (exit 1)

data: Every execution is recorded, so when a request fails you don’t need to re-run it with extra flags: look it up by id and compare it with the last time it worked.
data.1-get-the-execution-id#1. Get the execut:
A failed run prints it on stderr:
request failed: HTTP 500 (id: 078b9896) — inspect with: apigent diag 078b9896 Other ways to find it:
apigent history "health" # newest first, with short ids and errors apigent history "health" --json # [{"id","short_id","request","time","ok","status",...}] apigent timeline --since 1h # across all requests apigent run "health" --json | jq -r .short_id
data.2-inspect-it#2. Inspect it:
apigent diag 078b9896 # any unique prefix works; or: apigent diag --id 078b9896 diag shows:
Summary: result, status, failure phase (request_build, http, extraction, assertion, status, pre_request_script, post_response_script, run_if, next_request), duration, size Request as sent Variables, each with its variable origin (environment, collection, data, cli, or a runtime value) — secret values show as ***** Response headers and body (first 4KB; --full for all of it) Assertions Compared with last success: what changed since the last successful run of the same request — status, duration, URL, headers and body, variable values and origins, response headers and top-level JSON fields --json prints the record and the comparison as JSON.
data.3-read-the-failure-phase#3. Read the fai: Phase Usually means Next step request_build A placeholder couldn’t be filled Check the problems list; apigent run --dry-run http Connection error or timeout Host, network, --timeout status Non-2xx response Response body in diag; compare with last success assertion An --assert failed Assertion messages in diag extraction An --extract rule found nothing Test the rule with apigent extract on the stored body pre_request_script / post_response_script A script threw Script error in diag
data.compare-the-latest-responses#Compare the: apigent diff "health" # last two responses apigent diff "health" --json # structured RFC 6902 changes, or a text diff
data.secrets-in-records#Secrets in records: Records never contain secrets: secret and credential-looking values are masked before saving, so diag compares secret variables by origin only (“came from environment both times”), never by value. In agent mode, diag and diff also mask secrets in response bodies and headers, using the secrets of both compared runs.
data.see-also#See also: apigent diag, apigent history, apigent timeline, apigent diff
data.what-gets-recorded#What gets recorded:
Every execution of run (single requests, --chain steps, --data rows), collection run and shell send, including attempts that never got a response:
resolution problems (missing variables, bad types) connection errors and timeouts pre-request and post-response script errors failed assertions and non-2xx responses Dry runs are not recorded. Records store the method, URL, headers, body, variables with their origins, response headers, error, failure phase and assertion results, with secrets masked before saving. Response bodies are stored as received.

data: An environment is a named set of variables, such as BASE_URL and API_KEY, that fills the {{placeholders}} in saved requests at send time. Keep one environment per stage and the same saved requests work against all of them.
data.alias-keys-across-environments#Alias key:
Two environments may name the same credential differently. An alias is an environment value that refers to another key of the same environment:
apigent env set nets-beta 'API_KEY={{SA_KEY}}' Requests that use {{API_KEY}} now get the value of SA_KEY in nets-beta. Aliases resolve one level only (no re-expansion). When a request uses the alias, the resolved value is masked like the secret it points to.
data.create-an-environment#Create an environm: apigent env create dev --var BASE_URL=https://dev.api.example.com --var TIMEOUT=30 apigent env create prod --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com
data.environment-commands#Environment command: Command Description apigent env create Create an environment (--var KEY=VALUE, --var KEY=-, --secret KEY) apigent env list List environments (--json) apigent env show Show variables, secrets masked (--json, --reveal) apigent env set KEY=VALUE Set variables (KEY=- reads stdin) apigent env unset --var KEY Remove a variable apigent env switch Make an environment active apigent env import --file .env Import a .env file apigent env delete Delete an environment Full flags: apigent env. Next: Variables & placeholders explains how environment values combine with collection, data-row and --var values.
data.hand-an-environment-to-another-tool#Hand:
apigent exec runs a command with the environment’s variables in its process environment, without printing them:
apigent exec --env prod -- node e2e.mjs apigent exec --env prod -- sh -c 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$BASE_URL/v1/charges"'
data.store-a-secret-without-typing-it-on-the-:
Mark a variable secret with --secret KEY. Pass the value as KEY=- to read it from stdin; on a terminal apigent prompts without echo, so the value never lands in shell history:
apigent env create prod --var BASE_URL=https://api.example.com --var API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY # or later: apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY printf '%s' "$PROD_KEY" | apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY apigent env set prod KEY - (a lone -) is rejected: use KEY=-.
Secret values are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (see Credential storage) and shown as *****:
apigent env show prod # secrets masked apigent env show prod --json # {"name","id","variables":{...},"secrets":[...]}, masked apigent env show prod --reveal # plaintext; refused in agent mode apigent env list --json # [{"name","active","variables"}] --reveal prints secrets in plaintext to your terminal and its scrollback. Don’t use it while screen-sharing, in CI logs, or in a session an AI agent can read. It is refused in agent mode.
data.use-an-environment#Use an environment:
Reference variables as {{NAME}} in the URL, headers, body or auth params of a saved request:
apigent save "list-charges" '{{BASE_URL}}/v1/charges' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}' apigent run "list-charges" --env prod # one run apigent env switch prod # make prod the active environment apigent run "list-charges" --env with an unknown name is an error; apigent never silently runs without variables.

data: Saved requests are HTTP. For other protocols apigent has one-shot commands that take the endpoint as an argument. They are not saved, recorded, or filled from environments.
data.graphql#GraphQL: apigent graphql https://api.example.com/graphql --query '{ users { name email } }' apigent graphql https://api.example.com/graphql \ --query 'query($limit: Int!) { users(limit: $limit) { name } }' \ --vars '{"limit": 10}' apigent graphql https://api.example.com/graphql --query-file queries/get-users.graphql --op GetUsers To keep a GraphQL call with auth and environments, save it as an ordinary POST request with a JSON body ({"query": "...", "variables": {...}}) and run it with apigent run. Flags: apigent graphql.
data.grpc#gRPC: apigent grpc localhost:50051 --list # services via reflection apigent grpc localhost:50051 --service UserService --method GetUser --data '{"id": 1}' TLS options: --cacert, --cert, --key, --server-name, or --insecure for testing. Flags: apigent grpc.
data.server-sent-events#Server-Sent Events: apigent sse https://api.example.com/events --event order.created --json Flags: apigent sse.
data.websocket#WebSocket: apigent ws wss://echo.example.com --send '{"type":"ping"}' # send one message and exit apigent ws wss://echo.example.com --pretty --timestamp # interactive (stdin/stdout) Flags: apigent ws.

data: Assertions check a response without code; scripts run JavaScript before a request is sent and after its response arrives. Start with assertions and reach for a script only when you need logic.
data.assertions#Assertions:
Pass one or more --assert flags to run (all must pass), or save them on a request with apigent edit --assert:
apigent run "get-user" --assert "status=200" --assert "body.$.email contains @" apigent edit "get-user" --assert "status=200" A failed assertion makes run exit 1, records the execution with failure phase assertion, and prints the failure notice with the execution id. With --json, results are in "assertions":[{"name","passed","message"}].
data.example-capture-a-value-and-pick-the-nex: var data = apigent.response.json(); if (data.requiresProfile) { apigent.setVar("USER_ID", String(data.userId)); apigent.setNextRequest("get-profile"); }
data.example-validate-inside-a-script#Example: var data = apigent.response.json(); apigent.test("has users", function () { apigent.expect(data.status).to.equal("success"); });
data.examples#Examples: # Validation error is returned as expected apigent run "invalid-order" --assert "status=400" --assert "body contains validation" # Header present and fast enough apigent run "health" --assert "headers.X-Request-Id exists" --assert "time<500" # Extraction worked apigent run "login" --assert "extract:token != ''"
data.sandbox#Sandbox:
Scripts cannot read secret variables unless explicitly allowed, and URL changes are limited to http and https. See Security.
Tip Keep scripts small. If a script grows past a few lines, the logic probably belongs in your application or test code; use apigent exec to hand it an environment instead.
data.script-api#Script API:
Everything hangs off the global apigent object:
API Description apigent.request.headers.get(name) / .set(name, value) / .remove(name) Read or change request headers (pre-request) apigent.request.url, apigent.request.body, apigent.request.method Read or assign the URL, body and method apigent.response.status, .statusText, .time, .size, .body Response fields (post-response) apigent.response.json(), apigent.response.text() Parsed JSON body, raw text body apigent.response.headers.get(name) Response header apigent.setVar(name, value), apigent.getVar(name) Set or read a runtime variable apigent.setNextRequest(name) Run this saved request next (with run --chain or in a collection run) apigent.skipRequest() Skip the current request apigent.test(name, fn), apigent.expect(value).to.equal(expected) Named checks inside a script console.log, console.warn, console.error Logging Variables set with apigent.setVar are runtime values: the highest scope, available to later requests in the same run, and written back only with --persist (which refuses values containing {{). See Variables & placeholders.
data.scripts#Scripts:
Scripts are JavaScript (the goja runtime, ECMAScript 5.1+) saved on the request as inline source:
apigent save "login" '{{BASE_URL}}/login' -X POST --extract 'token=jsonpath:$.token' \ --post-script 'apigent.setNextRequest("profile")' apigent edit "profile" --pre-script 'apigent.request.headers.set("X-Request-Time", String(Date.now()))' Pre-request scripts run before the request is sent: add headers, rewrite the URL or body, or skip the request. Post-response scripts run after the response arrives: read the body, set variables, add tests, choose the next request.
data.see-also#See also: Chaining & extraction apigent run, apigent edit
data.syntax#Syntax:
Comparison operators attach directly to the field; word operators are surrounded by spaces:
status=200 status>=200 time<1000 body contains success body not_contains error body matches u-\d+ headers.X-Request-Id exists Operator Meaning =, != Equal, not equal <, >, <=, >= Numeric comparison contains, not_contains Substring match matches Regular expression match exists Field is present and non-empty (no value) Field Value status (or status_code) HTTP status code headers.NAME Response header, e.g. headers.Content-Type contains json body Whole response body as text body.$.path JSONPath into the body, e.g. body.$.data.items[0].id = 7 (body.data.id also works) extract:NAME A value extracted or set by a script, e.g. extract:orderId != '' time Response time in milliseconds size Response size in bytes An assertion that can’t be parsed (invalid assertion format) stops the run with exit code 1 before anything is sent.

data: A placeholder is a {{name}} marker in a saved request’s URL, headers, body or auth params. Request resolution replaces every placeholder with a value at send time, or stops the request and lists every problem. Nothing with an unresolved placeholder is ever sent.
data.dynamic-functions#Dynamic functions: Function Value {{$uuid}} Random UUID {{$timestamp}} Unix timestamp (seconds) {{$isoTimestamp}} ISO 8601 timestamp {{$randomInt(1,100)}} Random integer in the range {{$randomString(8)}} Random string of the given length {{$randomEmail}} Random email address Dynamic functions work in run, collection run, the shell and auth params. A dry run leaves them in place. An unknown function ({{$nope}}) is a resolution problem.
data.environment-aliases#Environment aliases: An environment value can name another key of the same environment: API_KEY={{SA_KEY}}. See Environments & secrets.
data.keeping-runtime-values---persist#Keeping:
Values extracted from a response (--extract) or set by a script (apigent.setVar) live only for the current run. Without --persist, run drops them and prints a note such as note: uid not saved; add --persist to use them in later runs.
With --persist, each extracted or script-set value is written back to its variable origin:
a variable that came from the environment goes to that environment (--env or the active one); otherwise it goes to the request’s collection, or to the environment if the request has no collection. --persist refuses:
a value that contains {{ (refusing to persist "tpl": value contains "{{"), so placeholders never get stored as values; a locked (passphrase-protected, not unlocked) collection, instead of overwriting it; --dry-run (exit code 2). CLI --var values and data-row values are never written back unless an extraction or a script changes them.
data.placeholder-forms#Placeholder forms: Form Meaning Example {{name}} Plain value, inserted as text {{BASE_URL}}/users/{{id}} {{name:num}} Must be a number {"amount": {{amount:num}}} {{name:bool}} Must be true or false {"live": {{live:bool}}} {{name:raw}} Inserted as-is (e.g. a JSON fragment) {"meta": {{meta:raw}}} {{$fn}} Dynamic function, computed per send {{$uuid}}
data.see-also#See also: Chaining & extraction apigent run and apigent docs (its “Placeholders” and “Scope precedence” sections are the short version of this page)
data.typed-placeholders-keep-json-bodies-vali:
A bare {{amount:num}} makes the stored body invalid JSON. Quote it instead: in a JSON body, the quoted form "{{amount:num}}" (likewise "{{x:bool}}" and "{{x:raw}}") drops the quotes when it is filled.
apigent save "charge" '{{BASE_URL}}/charges' -X POST \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"amount":"{{amount:num}}","capture":"{{capture:bool}}"}' apigent run "charge" --env dev --var amount=5 --var capture=true --dry-run POST https://dev.api.example.com/charges Content-Type: application/json {"amount":5,"capture":true} A value of the wrong type is a resolution problem (variable "amount" must be a number); the value itself is never echoed in the error.
data.when-resolution-fails#When resolution fa:
Every problem is collected and reported at once, and the request is not sent:
Error: variable substitution failed: missing required variables: BASE, API_KEY Problem kind Cause missing No scope has a value for {{name}} leftover_placeholder A value still contains a placeholder, e.g. --var 'API_KEY={{other}}'. Values are filled in one pass and never re-expanded. bad_type A typed placeholder got the wrong kind of value unknown_dynamic {{$fn}} is not a known function auth The auth config cannot be resolved With run --json, these appear as structured problems entries (kind, variable, location, message). Use --dry-run to check a request without sending it; it exits 1 when there are problems.
data.where-values-come-from-scopes#Where valu:
Each value comes from one scope. When the same name is set in several scopes, the higher one wins:
Scope (lowest first) Set with 1. Environment --env NAME or apigent env switch NAME 2. Collection apigent collection create/set-var (the request’s collection) 3. Data row --data rows.csv / rows.json 4. CLI --var key=value 5. Runtime values extracted from a response or set by a script earlier in the same run The scope a variable’s final value came from is its variable origin. apigent diag shows the origin of each variable in a recorded execution, and --persist uses it to decide where to write values back.
Collection values may reference environment keys, so one collection can serve several environments:
apigent env create staging --var BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com apigent collection create "users-api" --var 'API_URL={{BASE_URL}}/v1'

data:
apigent is built on one principle: credentials stay on your machine and out of anything apigent prints or stores.
Page Covers Credential storage AES-256-GCM encryption of environment and collection secrets, machine and collection keys, sharing secrets with a passphrase Secret masking What counts as a secret, where it is masked, --reveal, agent mode, execution records
data.code-generation-safety#Code generation s: All code generators (curl, Python, JavaScript, Go) escape values for the target language, preventing shell or code injection. codegen -l curl quotes each header as one argument (-H 'Content-Type: application/json'), masks literal secrets unless --reveal, and always replaces Authorization with a placeholder.
data.core-properties#Core properties:
Secrets are encrypted at rest. Environment and collection variables marked secret are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The machine key is generated with crypto/rand on first use and stored with owner-only permissions; encrypted values are useless on another machine.
Secrets are entered without echo. apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY reads the value from stdin, prompting without echo on a terminal.
Auth is applied inside apigent. Saved auth configs are filled from placeholders and applied to the outgoing request; the calling process never builds the credential string.
Output is masked. show, list --json, codegen, paste, env show, dry runs and run --json replace secrets with *****, including their URL- and JSON-escaped forms. Agent mode also masks response bodies, headers, errors and apigent exec child output.
Execution records never store secrets. Every run is recorded for apigent diag, with secrets masked before saving.
Layer What it handles Where secrets live Environment and collection secrets Encrypted storage and retrieval AES-256-GCM at rest Auth handlers Credential injection at send time In memory only Output and execution records Masked display and auditing Never: replaced with *****
data.path-protection#Path protection: Export and import commands validate file paths to prevent directory traversal; paths containing .. are rejected. Temporary files used during self-update are created with os.CreateTemp.
data.scripting-sandbox#Scripting sandbox: The JavaScript runtime restricts secret variable access by default: scripts cannot read secrets unless explicitly granted access. URL changes made by scripts are limited to http and https.

data: apigent separates secret storage from general configuration. Secrets are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM with a machine-specific key. General settings live in a plain TOML config file with no credentials.
data.auth-credentials-in-requests#Auth Creden:
Saved requests store auth configuration in a goleveldb database at ~/.local/share/apigent/apigent.db. Save or edit auth with --auth and repeated --auth-param key=value flags.
Database: goleveldb (LevelDB port, memory-mapped, transactional)
Auth params: Values are stored as JSON in SavedRequest.AuthConfig. If you put a literal password or token in --auth-param (or a literal Authorization header, or ?api_key=… in the URL), it is saved in the request database in plaintext. apigent masks such literals in show, list --json, codegen, paste and dry runs (see Secret masking), but masking is not encryption. Prefer placeholders that point at encrypted secrets, such as --auth-param token='{{API_TOKEN}}'.
Permissions: Database file has owner-only permissions by default
At execution time, apigent substitutes templates in auth parameters before the auth handler applies credentials to the outgoing request. Saved auth can be replaced with apigent edit --auth ... or cleared with apigent edit --auth none.
Future: Keychain integration for macOS and Windows is under consideration.
data.collection-secrets-encrypted#Collection:
Collection variables marked as secrets are encrypted with a per-collection AES-256-GCM key before they are written.
DB-backed collection key: ~/.local/share/apigent/keys/.key
File-backed collection key: .apigent/collections//collection.key
Git behavior: apigent init writes .apigent/.gitignore so collection.key files stay local. Commit collection.json and request files, but do not commit local collection keys.
Clone/share behavior:
Local use creates collection.key automatically when a collection secret is saved. A clone without collection.key can read non-secret collection variables and request files, but encrypted collection secrets remain locked. To share secrets, export the collection with a passphrase: apigent collection export --passphrase ... --output team.gurl. To migrate straight into shared project files, use apigent collection migrate --passphrase .... This writes passphrase-protected collection.json data and leaves no local collection.key. The receiver imports with the passphrase to re-encrypt secrets with that machine’s local collection.key, or unlocks a passphrase-protected file collection to cache the derived key in the OS keychain. Passphrase exports use PBKDF2-SHA256 with a per-export salt and AES-256-GCM for secret values. apigent collection unlock stores the derived key in the OS keychain so later commands can decrypt passphrase-protected collections without prompting again. --passphrase is available for interactive use, and APIGENT_IMPORT_PASSPHRASE can provide the passphrase in CI.
data.config-file#Config File:
The TOML config file at ~/.config/apigent/config.toml or ~/.apigentrc contains general settings only.
Stored settings:
history_depth (number of requests to keep in history) output_format (default output format) timeout (request timeout in seconds) log_level (logging verbosity) Never stored in config:

data.environment-secrets-encrypted#Environmen:
Environment variables marked --secret are encrypted before storage in both the default database and file-backed project environments under .apigent/environments/. This applies to API keys, OAuth tokens, passwords, and any other value you want protected.
Enter secrets without putting them on the command line: KEY=- reads the value from stdin, with a no-echo prompt on a terminal.
apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY Algorithm: AES-256-GCM
Machine key: 256-bit key generated via crypto/rand, stored at ~/.local/share/apigent/.secret-key with permissions 0600
Nonce: 12 bytes, randomly generated per encryption operation
Important Only values marked --secret get encrypted. Regular environment variables are stored as plaintext. Mark anything sensitive.
How it works:
First launch generates a 256-bit key using crypto/rand and saves it to ~/.local/share/apigent/.secret-key File permissions are set to 0600 (owner read/write only) When you create a secret: apigent env create prod --secret "API_KEY=sk-xxx", the value is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored At request execution time, the key is loaded, the value is decrypted, and templates such as {{API_KEY}} can be used by request fields or auth parameters The decrypted value lives only in memory during the request Machine dependency: Because the key is stored locally, encrypted values cannot be decrypted on a different machine. If you copy your apigent data to another machine, secrets are unreadable.
data.execution-records-no-secrets#Execution R: Every run is recorded in the same database so failures can be inspected with apigent diag. Records never contain secrets: secret and credential-looking values, literal credential headers and sensitive query parameters are masked before the record is written, as are their URL- and JSON-escaped copies in the URL, headers, body, errors and assertion messages. Response bodies are stored as received. See Secret masking.
data.security-comparison#Security Comparison: Concern apigent CLI AI Agent Direct Handling Credentials at rest Env secrets encrypted AES-256-GCM AI might store in plaintext context Credentials in transit Applied to headers by auth handlers AI might log/expose in prompts Output and records Secrets masked as ***** (bodies too in agent mode) AI might output full headers Machine key Per-machine 256-bit key (0600) AI has no equivalent Token caching OAuth2 tokens cached in memory with TTL AI might expose cached tokens The key difference is that apigent treats credential handling as a separate concern from request execution. Auth handlers apply credentials at the HTTP request layer, and templated auth params let saved requests refer to encrypted environment secrets instead of storing raw secret values in the request.

data: apigent replaces secret values with ***** in everything it prints or stores about a request. One set of rules (the internal/redact package) is shared by every command, so show, list --json, codegen, paste, dry runs, run --json and execution records all mask the same way.
data.execution-records-never-store-secrets#Ex: Every run is recorded so you can diagnose failures. Before a record is saved, secret variable values, literal credential headers and sensitive query parameters are masked, every occurrence of those values is scrubbed from the URL, request headers, request body, error and assertion messages, and sensitive response headers are masked. apigent diag therefore compares secret variables by origin only. Response bodies are stored as received.
data.request-logging#Request logging: The built-in logging plugin also replaces Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie and Proxy-Authorization header values with [REDACTED] in log output. The built-in user-agent plugin sets User-Agent: apigent/ when a request has none.

data.what-counts-as-a-secret#What counts as a:
A value is masked when any of these is true:
Rule Examples Its variable is marked secret in an environment or collection apigent env set prod API_KEY=- --secret API_KEY Its name looks sensitive Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, or any name containing key, secret, token, password, signature It is a literal value under a sensitive header -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-…' saved in the request It is a literal value of a sensitive query parameter https://api.example.com/v1?api_key=sk-live-… It is a literal sensitive auth param --auth-param token=…, the API key auth value, auth_code It was extracted or set by a script under a sensitive or secret name --extract access_token=jsonpath:$.token Every occurrence is replaced, not only the field it came from: if a secret appears in the URL, the body, an error message or an assertion message, it is masked there too, including its URL-escaped (%2B, +) and JSON-escaped (\", &) spellings. A secret overridden by a higher scope but still reachable through an alias is masked as well.
Values that still contain a {{placeholder}} only name a variable and stay visible, for example Authorization: Bearer {{API_KEY}}. Values shorter than 4 characters are not replaced inside free text, because that would garble unrelated text.
